# PulsHealth

> Sync Apple Health from your iPhone to a database you control. PulsHealth includes the iOS app, a self-hosted Docker Compose stack, a read-only API and MCP server, and an open sync protocol. The backend is pre-release. Source: https://github.com/PulsHealth/pulshealth. Website: https://pulshealth.com.

## Set up a server

Start with the [server setup guide](docs/setup.md). It is the step-by-step path for both people and coding assistants: prerequisites, a matching source/image version, phone connectivity, pairing, first-sync verification, and backups. Use the [server reference](server/README.md) only for configuration and operations details.

Copyable request:

> Help me set up PulsHealth using https://pulshealth.com/docs/setup/. First establish my server OS, Docker availability, time zone, and how my iPhone will reach it. Explain the plan, then work through setup and verify a first sync. Keep credentials out of chat. Ask before spending money, exposing a service publicly, or replacing existing data.

For setup agents:

- Inspect the existing installation before changing it. Preserve `server/.env`, volumes, and working services. Follow the guide's release/source-build choice; do not mix migrations from one revision with images from another.
- Configure a reachable phone URL. `localhost` on an iPhone is the iPhone; `--url` records an address and does not create HTTPS or a proxy. Keep the database, API, MCP, viewer and Grafana private unless deliberately configured otherwise.
- Bootstrap prints secrets and a pairing QR code. Keep its output local; do not copy tokens, `.env`, QR codes or health records into chat, logs or a public issue.
- A healthy container is only the server check. Separately verify the phone connection, an acknowledged sync, and the expected data in the viewer. Report anything still unverified.

## Read the docs

The site publishes plain Markdown at `https://pulshealth.com/docs/<slug>.md`, including [setup.md](https://pulshealth.com/docs/setup.md). [llms-full.txt](https://pulshealth.com/llms-full.txt) combines all published Markdown docs when a reader needs the complete reference. These are generated from the same repository sources as the human-readable pages. Read only the relevant guide first; deployed server behavior is described by the matching release's sources and its own `/openapi.json`.

- [Set up your server](docs/setup.md): the complete first-run workflow.
- [Server configuration and operations](server/README.md): services, networking, secrets, migrations, backups and upgrades.
- [Connect an AI assistant](docs/ai.md): query already-synced data through MCP or the API. This is separate from using a coding assistant to install the server.
- [Web viewer](web/README.md): dashboards, access and optional accounts.
- [Export data](docs/export.md): on-device files, server exports and the CLI.
- [Product API guide](docs/api.md): authentication, queries, pagination and errors.
- [API reference](server/api/openapi.json): machine-readable OpenAPI; also at https://pulshealth.com/openapi.json.
- [MCP reference](server/mcp/README.md): transports, configuration and read-only tools.

## Interpret the data

Read the [database guide](docs/database-guide.md) before writing SQL or drawing conclusions. Raw iPhone and Watch samples overlap; use `metric_daily` or the daily API for daily summaries. Wire timestamps are epoch milliseconds, quantity units are canonical, and missing data is not zero. MCP reads through the API, never directly from PostgreSQL.

- [Database guide](docs/database-guide.md): tables, query examples, calendars and double-counting traps.
- [Recording behavior](docs/recording-behavior.md): cadence, coverage, sources and sample intervals.
- [HealthKit knowledge base](knowledge-base/README.md): the source of https://pulshealth.com/knowledge-base/.

## Build an integration

- [Puls Sync Protocol v1](docs/protocol/README.md): implement a receiver; schemas, canonical units, idempotency and retries.
- [Type catalog](docs/protocol/catalog.json): generated HealthKit identifiers, kinds, units and allowed aggregate functions.
- [Catalog field guide](docs/protocol/catalog.md): meaning and generation of the vocabulary.
- [Python/SQLite receiver](examples/receivers/python-sqlite/README.md): a minimal alternative backend.
- [Swift package](PulsHealthSync/README.md): embed the sync engine in an iOS app.

## App and project

The [App Store app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pulshealth/id6757657354) can explore and export without a server. Free sync covers five types and the latest 30 days; Pro expands type and history access, subject to HealthKit permission and availability. Hosting is separate: run your own server or use a [hosted PulsHealth account](https://app.pulshealth.com/signup).

- [Project README](README.md): overview and component map.
- [Security](SECURITY.md): trust boundaries and private vulnerability reporting.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): backend release history.
- [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md): planned work and current limitations.
